# Abhijeet Rathore

> Personal site of Abhijeet Rathore, PhD researcher at IIT Roorkee (Department of Hydro and Renewable Energy) working on machine learning for solar and wind power forecasting in India. First author of a 2025 Renewable Energy (Elsevier) paper, co-inventor on a granted Indian patent, and builder of a live India-wide solar and wind forecasting app.

All pages on this site are prerendered static HTML, so their full text is readable without JavaScript. Every number on the site is sourced from the cited paper, the CV, the 2023 poster, or the app's published results file.

## Featured project: India Renewables Forecast (Jan to Mar 2026)

A forecasting platform that gives a solar and wind baseline for any location in India. Click a point on the map to get a 7-day generation forecast for your plant, with the first hours corrected by the latest satellite picture, alongside the long-term yield and project financials for that site. Built end to end: data, model, API and web app.

- Model: one India-wide LightGBM model predicts the clear-sky index (GHI / clear-sky GHI) to correct numerical weather prediction irradiance, with P10 / P90 quantile models for an 80% band. Satellite irradiance (NASA POWER) trains the model; at forecast time it needs only the weather forecast and sun geometry.
- Temperature: IMD gridded temperature corrects the forecast bias that feeds PV cell temperature and air density.
- Physics: pvlib clear-sky and PV modelling, hub-height wind extrapolation with hourly shear, and a turbine power curve.
- Satellite-corrected first hours: every hour the newest Meteosat-derived irradiance at the point (Open-Meteo satellite_radiation_seamless, about 2 h behind real time) is compared with the model; a debiased fraction (0.23) of the gap is added to the next hours, fading with a 4.75 h time constant and gone by 8 h. Fitted on training sites Jan to Jun 2025, scored at held-out sites Jul to Dec 2025 against NASA POWER: hourly RMSE 3.2% lower in the first live hour and 4.7% lower one hour after the reading. Next step: forecasting from cloud motion between consecutive images.
- From energy to rupees: deviation charges under the GERC 2019 bands (replaying 2024, scheduling on the model cuts them by about 42% on average across the 32 test sites), and project NPV, IRR, LCOE and payback from the plant's P50/P90 yield, with defaults cited from KERC tariff orders, SECI auction tariffs and CERC norms. Both open a step-by-step calculation.
- Testing: trained on 2022 to 2023, scored on all of 2024. Hourly irradiance RMSE at training sites fell from 101 to 78 W/m2 (23% better than the raw forecast); 10% better at 8 sites held out of training entirely; a similar gain holds through the monsoon. The app shows where the model struggles (for example high-altitude Leh) rather than hiding it.
- Stack: Python, LightGBM, pvlib, pandas, FastAPI, React, Leaflet, Render, Vercel, GitHub Actions.
- Live results files the case study reads: https://app.abhijeetrathore.in/data/model_results.json and https://app.abhijeetrathore.in/data/sat_nowcast.json

## Research highlight: day-ahead solar forecasting with FFT-assisted LSTM

Rathore, Gupta, Sharma and Singh, "Day ahead solar forecast using long short term memory network augmented with Fast Fourier transform-assisted decomposition technique", Renewable Energy 247 (2025) 123021. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2025.123021 (not open access; the DOI is the canonical link).

- Role: first author (software, data curation, analysis, validation, figures, first draft).
- Method: NA-MEMD decomposes multivariate weather series (temperature, humidity, wind speed and direction, solar zenith angle; NSRDB 2005 to 2014) into 14 to 15 intrinsic mode functions; an FFT groups them by dominant frequency into 5 signals (HIGH 1 to 3, MEDIUM, LOW); one attention-based LSTM per signal forecasts the next day's 11 sunshine hours; the forecasts are summed.
- Sites: Jodhpur (hot-dry), Kamuthi (warm-humid), Chikkoppa (warm-humid), Charanka (hot-dry).
- Results (Table 5, test-set RMSE in W/m2 for AM-LSTM / N-AM-LSTM / proposed): Jodhpur 91.22 / 69.22 / 67.52; Kamuthi 121.26 / 71.5 / 51.89; Chikkoppa 107.47 / 87.36 / 70.12; Charanka 88.49 / 63.87 / 62.38. Mean RMSE 62.97 W/m2 (nRMSE 6.33%, R 0.972): 36.9% lower than attention-LSTM alone and 13% lower than decomposition without FFT.
- Training time (Section 4.3): 876 s versus 2128 s for N-AM-LSTM, 58.8% less, by training 5 models instead of 15.
- Stack: Python, Keras and TensorFlow, Keras Tuner, scikit-learn, Matplotlib.

## Earlier research projects

- M.Tech thesis: Yield Modelling and Data-Driven Feasibility Analysis of Solar PV and Solar Thermal Systems. Data-driven PV energy yield model with integrated optimisation for site-specific feasibility and parameter tuning (MATLAB, statistics).
- B.Tech project: Enhancement of Voltage Quality in Isolated Power Systems. Battery-backed series compensator in MATLAB/Simulink to reduce total harmonic distortion and improve voltage stability.
- Training: UPPCL Lucknow (132 kV substation operations); Industrial Automation workshop, Sofcon (PLC, HMI, SCADA); UNICON PLC Automation (MATLAB control systems, signal processing).

## Skills

- Machine learning: Python, time-series forecasting, physics-informed machine learning, mixture of experts (model routing and blending), LSTM and attention, LightGBM, scikit-learn, TensorFlow / Keras, feature engineering.
- LLMs and edge AI: fine-tuning large language models (Gemma, Llama, Qwen) for time-series forecasting with LoRA and QLoRA (PyTorch, Hugging Face), llama.cpp, prompt engineering, knowledge distillation, lightweight models, Raspberry Pi, sensor integration.
- Energy modelling: pvlib, solar PV yield, wind power curves, NWP and satellite data, signal decomposition (EMD, FFT), MATLAB / Simulink.
- Engineering: FastAPI, Flask, Streamlit, React, data pipelines, GitHub Actions, Vercel / Render.
